req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with the same body for the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states PUT /tasks/{task_id} must be idempotent: repeating the same PUT with the same body must yield the same terminal state. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — two identical PUTs produce identical response bodies and HTTP 200; (2) negative NEG — PUT to a non-existent task_id returns 404 on every call; (3) boundary BVA — PUT with a title at the max-length boundary (100 chars) is idempotent; (4) STC — state transition from incomplete→complete is stable across repeated PUTs; (5) DT — PUT with all optional fields supplied is idempotent. Each test asserts exact field values to kill constant-mutation, operator-flip, and boolean-negation mutants.

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_same_response_twice
preconditions: Task with id=7 exists: title='Fix login bug', completed=false
Database is in the pre-loaded state
actions: PUT /tasks/7 with body {title: 'Fix login bug updated', completed: true}
expected: r1 and r2 have identical id, title, description, completed fields
title == 'Fix login bug updated' in both responses
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_put_idempotent_same_response_twice():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Fix login bug updated", "completed": True}
    r1 = client.put("/tasks/7", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    body1 = r1.json()
    assert body1["id"] == 7
    assert body1["title"] == "Fix login bug updated"
    assert body1["completed"] is True

    r2 = client.put("/tasks/7", json=payload)
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert body2["id"] == 7
    assert body2["title"] == "Fix login bug updated"
    assert body2["completed"] is True

    assert body1["id"] == body2["id"]
    assert body1["title"] == body2["title"]
    assert body1["description"] == body2["description"]
    assert body1["completed"] == body2["completed"]

tests.name: test_put_nonexistent_task_returns_404_idempotently
preconditions: Task with id=9999 does not exist in the pre-loaded dataset
expected: Both response bodies contain detail message referencing task id 9999
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_put_nonexistent_task_returns_404_idempotently():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Ghost task", "completed": False}
    r1 = client.put("/tasks/9999", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == 404
    detail1 = r1.json()["detail"]
    assert "9999" in detail1

    r2 = client.put("/tasks/9999", json=payload)
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    detail2 = r2.json()["detail"]
    assert "9999" in detail2

    assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code
    assert detail1 == detail2

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_title_at_max_length_boundary
preconditions: Task with id=10 exists: title='Organize desk', completed=false
Max title length is 100 characters per schema
actions: Construct a title string of exactly 100 characters
PUT /tasks/10 with the identical 100-char title again
Assert both responses are 200 with identical title field
expected: title in both responses equals the 100-character string exactly
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_put_idempotent_title_at_max_length_boundary():
    client = TestClient(app)
    max_title = "A" * 100
    assert len(max_title) == 100
    payload = {"title": max_title, "completed": False}

    r1 = client.put("/tasks/10", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    body1 = r1.json()
    assert body1["title"] == max_title
    assert len(body1["title"]) == 100
    assert body1["completed"] is False
    assert body1["id"] == 10

    r2 = client.put("/tasks/10", json=payload)
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert body2["title"] == max_title
    assert len(body2["title"]) == 100
    assert body2["completed"] is False
    assert body2["id"] == 10

    assert body1["title"] == body2["title"]
    assert body1["completed"] == body2["completed"]

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_state_transition_incomplete_to_complete
preconditions: Task with id=4 exists: title='Prepare meeting agenda', completed=false
actions: Verify initial state via GET /tasks/4 shows completed=false
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_put_idempotent_state_transition_incomplete_to_complete():
    client = TestClient(app)
    get0 = client.get("/tasks/4")
    assert get0.status_code == 200
    assert get0.json()["completed"] is False
    assert get0.json()["id"] == 4

    payload = {"title": "Prepare meeting agenda", "completed": True}
    r1 = client.put("/tasks/4", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r1.json()["completed"] is True
    assert r1.json()["id"] == 4
    assert r1.json()["title"] == "Prepare meeting agenda"

    r2 = client.put("/tasks/4", json=payload)
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r2.json()["completed"] is True
    assert r2.json()["id"] == 4
    assert r2.json()["title"] == "Prepare meeting agenda"

    get_final = client.get("/tasks/4")
    assert get_final.status_code == 200
    assert get_final.json()["completed"] is True
    assert get_final.json()["id"] == 4

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_all_fields_supplied
preconditions: Task with id=5 exists: title='Write project report', completed=false
actions: PUT /tasks/5 with all optional fields: title, description, completed
PUT /tasks/5 with identical body a second time
Assert both responses have identical id, title, description, completed
expected: title == 'Write project report revised' in both
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_put_idempotent_all_fields_supplied():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {
        "title": "Write project report revised",
        "description": "Updated description text.",
        "completed": True
    }
    r1 = client.put("/tasks/5", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == 200

    assert b1["id"] == 5
    assert b1["title"] == "Write project report revised"
    assert b1["description"] == "Updated description text."
    assert b1["completed"] is True

    r2 = client.put("/tasks/5", json=payload)
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    b2 = r2.json()
    assert b2["id"] == 5
    assert b2["title"] == "Write project report revised"
    assert b2["description"] == "Updated description text."
    assert b2["completed"] is True

    assert b1["id"] == b2["id"]
    assert b1["title"] == b2["title"]
    assert b1["description"] == b2["description"]
    assert b1["completed"] == b2["completed"]

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_title_one_over_max_rejected
preconditions: Max title length is 100 characters; 101 chars must be rejected
expected: Task state is unchanged (GET /tasks/6 still has original title)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_put_idempotent_title_one_over_max_rejected():
    client = TestClient(app)
    over_title = "B" * 101
    assert len(over_title) == 101
    payload = {"title": over_title, "completed": False}

    r1 = client.put("/tasks/6", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == 422

    r2 = client.put("/tasks/6", json=payload)
    assert r2.status_code == 422

    get_r = client.get("/tasks/6")
    assert get_r.status_code == 200
    assert get_r.json()["title"] == "Run unit tests"
    assert get_r.json()["completed"] is False
